title: On exit: ERROR: Pages in use exist at exit in PagedAllocator
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in Godot v4.5.beta2, Godot v4.5.beta3, Godot v4.5.rc2

### System information

Godot v4.5.beta3 - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6119) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800H with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 15.34 GiB memory

### Issue description

A seemingly innocuous code change in my project triggers this error 100% consistently on exit:

```
ERROR: Pages in use exist at exit in PagedAllocator: N7Variant5Pools12BucketMediumE
   at: ~PagedAllocator (./core/templates/paged_allocator.h:169)
```

I think this points to a memory leak or memory corruption in the script parser, but unfortunately I don't have a minimal repro.

### Steps to reproduce

File `level_tree_global.gd` is included in the `autoload` list in `godot.project`. This is the entire contents of that file:
```gdscript
extends Node
var level: LevelGraphNode
```

`LevelGraphNode` is a custom class that extends `Control`. If `level_tree_global.gd` is amended to have no references to `LevelGraphNode` (e.g. changing the variable definition to `var level: Control`), the error does not occur. If `level_tree_global.gd` is removed from the `[autoload]` section of `godot.project`, the error does not occur.

By commenting out large parts of `LevelGraphNode` and other files indirectly referenced, I was able to narrow the problem down to a class `PieceReference`. If there are no references to `PieceReference` from the autoloaded file, the PagedAllocator error does not occur. This is the entire contents of the `PieceReference` file:
```gdscript
class_name PieceReference
extends Resource

@export var original_transform: Transform3D

static func this_function_causes_the_problem() -> PieceReference:
    return PieceReference.new()
```

The function `this_function_causes_the_problem` is not called or referenced from any other code in the project. This file seems to be very brittle; small changes prevent the error from occuring:
* If the `this_function_causes_the_problem` function definition is deleted, the error stops happening.
* If the body of the function is replaced with `return null`, the error stops happening.
* If the keyword `@export` is deleted from the definition of `original_transform`, the error stops happening.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I tried to repro in a minimal project, but unfortunately haven't been able to yet. I'm not willing to publicly share the full project code, but I'm happy to share with an individual contributor interested in investigating.
